analysis.summary: A must-win Group J contest for both sides after opening defeats: Jordan lost 3-1 to Austria and Algeria were beaten 3-0 by Argentina. Algeria carry significantly greater technical quality — a 4-3-3 built around Mahrez, Amoura and Gouiri, all playing at high European club level — while Jordan are a compact, counter-attacking side in their first-ever World Cup who scored a historic goal against Austria from a disciplined 3-4-3 shape. A further defeat for either side would all but end their qualification hopes with Argentina and Austria still to come.
analysis.home_form: Jordan qualified for the World Cup for the first time in their history, topping AFC qualification and reaching the 2025 Arab Cup final (lost 3-2 to Morocco). At the World Cup, they lost their debut match 3-1 to Austria but showed spirit — Ali Olwan's 50th-minute strike was Jordan's first-ever World Cup goal. Key injury: Yazan Al Naimat (eight qualifying goals) remains out since December with injury. Ibrahim Sabra also withdrew pre-tournament. No suspension concerns reported.
analysis.away_form: Algeria reached the World Cup under Vladimir Petkovic after a strong AFC qualification where Mohamed Amoura finished as leading scorer with 10 goals. Pre-tournament friendlies included a 4-0 win over Bolivia and 7-0 over Guatemala. At the World Cup, they suffered a 3-0 defeat to Argentina in the opener, a harsh scoreline partly disputed by the FAF who filed a formal complaint with FIFA over refereeing (Messi and Mac Allister incidents). Ismael Bennacer was a pre-tournament injury omission (hamstring). No fresh suspensions confirmed.
analysis.h2h: The two nations have met just three times: Algeria beat Jordan 6-0 in a 1974 regional tournament; Jordan won 2-1 at the 1988 Arab Cup; the most recent meeting was a 1-1 friendly in May 2004. No meaningful competitive precedent exists. Algeria lead the historical series 1W-1D-1L.
injuries_news: Jordan: Yazan Al Naimat (top qualifying scorer, 8 goals) absent since December with injury — confirmed out of tournament.
Jordan: Ibrahim Sabra withdrew from squad pre-tournament, replaced by Mohammad Taha.
Algeria: Ismael Bennacer absent from squad (hamstring injury, suffered during AFCON).
Algeria: No fresh matchday 1 injuries or suspensions confirmed.
Jordan: No fresh matchday 1 injuries or suspensions confirmed.
key_factors: Existential pressure: a defeat for either team would leave them needing a near-miraculous swing on Matchday 3 against stronger opponents (Jordan face Argentina, Algeria face Austria), making this effectively a knockout match.

Algeria's 4-3-3 attacking frontline of Mahrez, Amoura and Gouiri represents a significant quality gap over Jordan's back three, though Jordan's defensive organization held Austria scoreless for 76 minutes before the match opened up.

Jordan's counter-attacking threat is real — Musa Al-Taamari and Ali Olwan can hurt Algeria with pace on transitions, and Jordan's compact 3-back shape may make life difficult for Petkovic's side in the early stages.

The 3-0 scoreline vs Argentina may understate Algeria's true level given disputed refereeing decisions; they are likely to be strongly motivated and better-organized against a Jordan side they will view as beatable.
Levi's Stadium is a neutral venue in California; no significant altitude, heat or travel advantage for either side.
Opta's pre-match simulation (25,000 runs) gives Algeria 60.1%, draw 22.2%, Jordan 17.7% — consistent with the market odds.
